last_transition_reason: The submitted proof is empty, and the supplied counterexample family can be made rigorous. Fix d=r=1 and let B be any proposed uniform X-support bound. Take n=2B+13, which is admissible since n is odd. If C(X,q)=∑_{j=-B}^B c_j(q)X^j satisfied the telescoping identities for k=1,...,n-1, then with X=q^k those identities become 1 = C(X,q) - R(X,q) C(qX,q), where R(X,q)=q^{-1}X^{-1}(1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)/((1-qX^3)(1+qX)). After clearing denominators, F(X,q):=qX(1-qX^3)(1+qX)C(X,q) - (1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)C(qX,q) - qX(1-qX^3)(1+qX) is a Laurent polynomial in X with exponents contained in [-B,B+10], hence with at most 2B+11 X-monomials. But F(q^k,q)=0 for k=1,...,n-1=2B+12. Since the q^k are distinct over Q(q), the resulting Vandermonde system forces F(X,q)≡0. Now compare highest X-degree terms: if m is the largest exponent with c_m(q)≠0, then the second term contributes a nonzero X^{m+10} term q^{m+8}c_m(q)X^{m+10}, while the first term has X-degree at most m+5 and the final term has degree at most 5. So F cannot vanish identically. Contradiction. Therefore no such uniformly bounded-support certificate exists; the lemma statement is false.
role_in_parent: This is the single theorem-specific input: a structured bounded-support telescoping certificate for the original finite sum difference.
statement_nl:
Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-a q^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d. Then there exists a nonnegative integer B such that for every integer n > 1 satisfying n ≡ 1 mod 2d there exists a Laurent polynomial in X over Z[q^±1] of the form C_{d,r,n}(X,q) = ∑_{j=-B}^{B} c_j(q) X^j, with each c_j(q) in Z[q^±1], having the following property. Define the modulus M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n define
T_{d,r,n,k}(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k,
and define
G_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q) · C_{d,r,n}(q^k,q).
Also define
H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2},
and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 define
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q).
Then H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for every integer k with 0 <= k <= n-1, and there exist polynomials A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1, gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1, G_{d,r,n,0}(q) = M_n(q) A_0(q) / B_0(q), and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) = M_n(q) A_n(q) / B_n(q).

domain_restrictions: d and r are fixed positive integers.
n is an integer greater than 1.
k is an integer with 0 <= k <= n when the definitions are made.
The telescoping identity is required only for 0 <= k <= n - 1.
C_{d,r,n}(X,q) has X exponents only from -B to B.
Each coefficient c_j(q) lies in integer Laurent polynomials in q.
A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) lie in polynomials in q with integer coefficients.
gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1 and gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1 are required in the polynomial ring in q.
The endpoint formulas for G_{d,r,n,0}(q) and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) are rational-function equalities with the stated coprimality conditions.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For fixed positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r) = 1 and r <= d, there is a uniform nonnegative bound B such that every integer n greater than 1 and congruent to 1 modulo 2d admits a Laurent polynomial C_{d,r,n}(X,q) whose X exponents lie between -B and B and whose coefficients are integer Laurent polynomials in q. With this choice, the associated terms G_{d,r,n,k}(q) satisfy a telescoping relation H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for all k from 0 to n - 1, and the boundary values G_{d,r,n,0}(q) and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) can be written as M_n(q) times a polynomial divided by a polynomial coprime to M_n(q).
quantifier_order: Fix d and r as positive integers with gcd(d,r) = 1 and r <= d.
There exists a nonnegative integer B that does not depend on n.
For every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, there exists a Laurent polynomial C_{d,r,n}(X,q) of the form sum over j from -B to B of c_j(q) times X^j.
For every integer k with 0 <= k <= n, define T_{d,r,n,k}(q), G_{d,r,n,k}(q), and H_{d,r,n,k}(q).
For every integer k with 0 <= k <= n - 1, the telescoping identity H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) holds.

For each admissible n, there exist polynomials A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) such that gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1, gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1, G_{d,r,n,0}(q) = M_n(q) times A_0(q) divided by B_0(q), and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) = M_n(q) times A_n(q) divided by B_n(q).

For each admissible n, C_{d,r,n}(X,q) may depend on d, r, and n, but not on k.
The coefficients c_j(q) are the coefficients of the chosen C_{d,r,n}(X,q) and therefore inherit its dependence on d, r, and n.
A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) are existential witnesses for each admissible n and may depend on d, r, and n, but not on k.
G_{d,r,n,k}(q) depends on the chosen C_{d,r,n}(X,q) and on T_{d,r,n,k}(q).
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) is defined directly from T_{d,r,n,k}(q) and does not introduce new witnesses.
